login.title: Sign in — authentication service
login.heading: Sign in
login.linkAccount: Link your account. A federation partner signed you in as {name}, and that account is not linked to it yet. Sign in here as {name} to link them; Cancel links nothing.
login.passkeysOff: Passkeys are switched off in this realm (webauthn.enabled), so neither passkey option is offered. A passkey already registered still works.
login.keySecond: Use a passkey as a second step (WebAuthn)
login.keySecondNotAvailable: — not available: this partner is configured for a passkey instead of a password
login.keySecondRequiredSecond: — required after a password: this request demands a passkey as the second factor
login.keySecondRequired: — required after a password: this request demands a passkey, alone or as the second factor
login.keySecondOff: A passkey as a second step is switched off here (webauthn.mfaAllowed).
login.keyOnly: Sign in with a passkey instead of a password (no password step, and the tokens will say one factor)
login.keyOnlyAccepted: — accepted: this request demands a passkey
login.keyOnlyNotAvailable: — not available: this request demands two factors
login.keyOnlyRequiredRelationship: — required: the federation relationship "{name}" configures this
login.keyOnlyRequiredApplication: — required: the application allows a passkey alone on this screen
login.keyOnlyOff: A passkey instead of a password is switched off here (webauthn.primaryAllowed).
login.keyOnlyCannotComplete: This sign-in cannot complete: the federation relationship "{name}" configures a mechanism this realm has turned off.
login.rememberNote: — recognises it next time with a cookie. Do not tick on a shared computer.
login.anonymousTitle: Continue as the anonymous principal. The flow goes on and tokens may be issued, but the session records that nobody authenticated — so an application requiring ALL_AUTHENTICATED_USERS will refuse it. Anything typed above is ignored.
login.noScreen: This application is not signed in to on this screen. Use one of the ways it allows, below.
login.metaChecked: Your password is checked against your account.
login.metaPasswordlessChecked: Passwordless: the password field is not read, and a passkey you registered is the only factor. A passkey is added at /portal/keys after signing in, never here.
login.metaUnchecked: No password is checked. The username you enter is the identity the issued tokens describe.
login.metaPasswordlessUnchecked: Passwordless: the password field is not read at all, and the passkey becomes the only factor — a passkey is registered for this username on first use, so the first person to claim a name here gets it. This service authenticates nobody; that is the same statement as the line above and not a weaker one.
login.metaPasskey: Sign in with a passkey: no username — the passkey names your account, and it must verify you with its PIN or biometric, so the tokens say two factors (amr ["hwk","user"], acr "mfa").
options.federatedOwnMany: This application signs its users in at one of these federated identity providers. Pick the one you have an account at. No password is typed here and none is checked there either as far as this service can tell — what it checks is the partner's signature.
options.federatedOwnOne: This application signs its users in at a federated identity provider. No password is typed here and none is checked there either as far as this service can tell — what it checks is the partner's signature.
options.federatedAny: Or sign in with a federated identity provider. No password is typed here and none is checked there either as far as this service can tell — what it checks is the partner's signature.
options.kerberosWithheldKey: Integrated Kerberos sign-in is not offered for this request: it demands a passkey.
options.kerberosWithheldMfa: Integrated Kerberos sign-in is not offered for this request: it demands two factors, and a ticket claims whatever its own flags claim — usually one.
options.kerberos: Or sign in with a Kerberos ticket, if this machine holds one. Nothing is typed and this service checks the ticket rather than a name — the only sign-in here that rests on a credential it genuinely verified.
options.walletWithheld: Signing in with a wallet is not offered for this request: it demands a security key.
options.wallet: Or sign in with a wallet that holds a credential this service issued to you. Nothing is typed: your wallet proves it holds the key the credential is bound to.
options.walletMfaNote: This request needs two factors, so you will be asked for a second one afterwards unless your wallet's key is attested to need your PIN or biometric.
options.siopButton: Sign in with a self-issued ID
options.certificate: Or continue with the TLS client certificate your browser presented on this connection. Nothing is typed: this service checked the certificate's chain and whether it has been revoked.
options.certificateMfaNote: This request needs two factors, so you will be asked for a second one afterwards.
selectIdp.title: Choose how to sign in — authentication service
selectIdp.heading: Choose how to sign in
selectIdp.blurbNamed: {application} signs its users in at one of these federated identity providers. Pick the one you have an account at. No password is typed here and none is checked there either as far as this service can tell — what it checks is the partner's signature.
selectIdp.blurb: This application signs its users in at one of these federated identity providers. Pick the one you have an account at. No password is typed here and none is checked there either as far as this service can tell — what it checks is the partner's signature.
selectIdp.meta: These are the relationships named on this application's entry under ou=applications, in appFederationRelationship — not every federation relationship this service has.
passwordChange.title: Choose a new password — authentication service
passwordChange.heading: Choose a new password
passwordChange.sub: The password for {name} was set for you and must be changed before you continue.
passwordChange.meta: Nothing has been signed in yet. The sign-in you started continues as soon as the new password is stored.
mfaSetup.title: Set up a second factor
mfaSetup.heading: Set up a second factor
mfaSetup.subProved: The application you are signing in to does not accept the second factor you just gave for {name}. Set up one it does accept; nothing is signed in until you have.
mfaSetup.subRecovery: {name} was recovered without its passkey, and this realm lets it reach no application until a passkey has signed you in. Register a new passkey here; you will then sign in with it. Nothing is signed in until you do.
mfaSetup.subOptional: You hold an administrator role, and {name} has no second factor yet. Setting one up now is recommended; you can ignore this and sign in with your password, and you will be asked again next time.
mfaSetup.subRequired: A second factor is required for {name}, and you do not have one yet. Nothing is signed in until one is set up.
mfaSetup.totpText: A six-digit code from an app such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password or any other RFC 6238 app.
mfaSetup.passkeyText: A passkey on this device, your phone or a security key, used after your password.
mfaSetup.ignoreText: Sign in with your password alone.
mfaSetup.meta: This step expires in a few minutes; if it does, sign in again from the application that sent you here.
mfaSetup.scanHeading: Scan this with your authenticator app
mfaSetup.scanSub: For {name}. Nothing is stored until the code below checks out.
mfaSetup.qrAlt: QR code carrying this account's otpauth setup URI
mfaSetup.typeIt: Or type it in: {secret} ({algorithm}, {digits} digits, every {period} seconds)
mfaSetup.codeLabel: The {digits}-digit code your app shows now
webauthn.title: Passkey — authentication service
webauthn.subPasswordless: Signing in as {name} with a passkey instead of a password
webauthn.subSecond: Second step for {name}: use your passkey
webauthn.laneClassicalWhat: ES256 or RSA — what nearly every authenticator can make.
webauthn.lanePqcWhat: ML-DSA, listed as a second account ending in “+ml-dsa”. Few authenticators can make one yet.
webauthn.unsupported: Your device could not make a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey, which this service asks for first.
webauthn.maybeUnsupported: If your device could not make a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey, you can make a classical one instead.
webauthn.cannotMake: This service requires a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey, and this device could not make one. Use another device, or a security key that can.
webauthn.maybeCannotMake: If your device could not make the passkey: this service requires a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey. Use another device, or a security key that can.
webauthn.hybrid: Your browser can also make the passkey on a phone or another device nearby: choose that when it asks.
webauthn.retryClassical: Try again with a classical passkey
webauthn.retryClassicalWhat: A classical passkey (ES256 or RSA) is what nearly every device can make.
pqRequired.heading: This application requires a post-quantum passkey
pqRequired.text: The passkey you used signs with a classical algorithm, and this application accepts only a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey. You were not signed in.
pqRequired.how: Use a post-quantum passkey if you have one. Otherwise add one on your account page, signing in there another way, and come back.
webauthn.noPrompt: My browser did not ask — tell me why
webauthn.rpId: RP ID: {rpId} — the ceremony is bound to this origin.
webauthn.rpIdWidened: RP ID: {rpId} — the ceremony is bound to this origin, widened to this suffix by webauthn.rpId.
webauthn.uvChecked: (CHECKED here — an authenticator that did not verify is refused)
webauthn.modeCreate: No passkey is registered for this user yet, so this step registers one.
webauthn.modeGet: A passkey is already registered for this user, so this step is an assertion.
webauthn.amrPasswordless: No password was presented. On success the session records amr ["hwk"] and acr "1" — ONE factor — and this counts as an authentication in its own right, so it appears on /admin/users and the directory grows an entry for {name}.
webauthn.amrSecond: A password step has already succeeded. On success the session records amr ["pwd","hwk"] and acr "mfa", and the directory entry for {name} is flagged as having authenticated with more than one factor.
webauthn.backup: I do not have my passkey — use a recovery code
totp.title: One-time code — authentication service
startOver.note: Back to the sign-in screen for the same request. Nothing from this step is kept.
stuck.close: Close this browser tab or window and start over.
totp.heading: Your one-time code
totp.label: The {digits}-digit code from your authenticator app
totp.meta: The code changes every {period} seconds. A code can only be used once (RFC 6238 section 5.2), so if you have just signed in, wait for the next one.
totp.backup: I cannot use my authenticator app — use a recovery code
backupCode.title: Recovery code — authentication service
backupCode.heading: Use a recovery code
backupCode.sub: Instead of {factor, select, passkey {your passkey} code {the emailed code} link {the emailed link} other {your authenticator app}}, for {name}
backupCode.low: Only {remaining} of your {total} recovery codes are unused. A set is issued once and is never topped up — after the last one an administrator has to clear the set before a new one can be issued.
backupCode.label: One of the recovery codes you were given
backupCode.once: Each code works once. The dashes and the case do not matter — type it however you can read it.
backupCode.back: Go back and use {factor, select, passkey {your passkey} code {the emailed code} link {the emailed link} other {your authenticator app}} after all
passwordFactor.title: Your password — authentication service
passwordFactor.heading: Your password
passwordFactor.sub: Second factor for {name}, after your wallet.
passwordFactor.meta: Your wallet has already presented a credential this service issued to you. On success the session records amr {amr} and acr "mfa".
secondFactor.totpInstead: Use a code from your authenticator app instead
secondFactor.emailLinkInstead: Email me a sign-in link instead
home.title: Continue signing in
home.text: Your account is held in another region of this service. Continue to sign in there.
accounts.title: Choose an account — authentication service
accounts.heading: Choose an account
accounts.blurb: This browser is signed in to more than one account. Choose the one to continue with, or sign in with another account.
accounts.blurbNamed: Choose the account to continue to {application} with, or sign in with another account.
accounts.full: This browser is signed in to {max} accounts, the most it may hold. Sign out of one of them to use another.
postLogin.title: One more step — authentication service
postLogin.heading: Register a post-quantum passkey
postLogin.subClassical: {name}, your passkey is made with a classical algorithm. Register a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey as well; the passkey you have keeps working.
postLogin.subNone: {name}, register a passkey: a post-quantum (ML-DSA) one.
postLogin.device: Your device or browser has to be able to make an ML-DSA passkey. If it cannot, the registration fails and nothing changes.
postLogin.required: The time allowed for this has passed: register the passkey to finish signing in.
postLogin.until: You can skip this until {date}; after that it is required.
postLogin.subUpgrade: {name}, your passkey is made with a classical algorithm. Upgrade it to a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey.
postLogin.methodUpgrade: You use your current passkey once, to show it is yours, and then create the post-quantum passkey on the same authenticator. It replaces the old one there, so you keep one passkey.
postLogin.methodSeparate: Create it on a different authenticator from the one that holds your current passkey — a security key that supports ML-DSA, for example.
postLogin.proofSub: Use the passkey {name} once, to show it is yours. The post-quantum passkey is created next, on the same authenticator.
postLogin.subAttestation: {name}, your post-quantum passkey was not attested with post-quantum algorithms. Register one that is.
postLogin.failed: Your device did not create the passkey ({error}).
postLogin.failedHelp: If your device or browser cannot make an ML-DSA passkey, register it on a separate security key that supports ML-DSA, or ask an administrator: where your passkey policy lets an administrator enrol a passkey for you, they can register one, and they can upgrade your passkey from the console.
postLogin.failedSkip: You can also skip this for now.
